'''''Linaria repens''''', also known as '''pale toadflax''' or '''creeping toadflax''' in Europe and as '''striped toadflax''' in the US, is an herbaceous plant in the family [[Plantaginaceae]], native to Europe.<ref name="rhs">{{cite web|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/58211/Linaria-repens/Details|title=Linaria repens | creeping toadflax/RHS Gardening|website=rhs.org.uk|accessdate=2019-06-11}}</ref>

==Description==

''Linaria repens'' is a short-statured herb (maximum 80 cm), spreading by rhizomes. Upper flower petals are pale with purple veins. Lower petals are pale purple-white, usually with a yellow centre. Its appearance is similar to ''[[Linaria purpurea]]'', and the flowers closely resemble ''[[Cymbalaria muralis]]'' so care must be taken in identification.<ref name="naturespot">{{cite web|url=https://www.naturespot.org.uk/node/126819|title=Pale Toadflax|website=NatureSpot|accessdate=2019-06-11}}</ref><ref name="genialvegetal">{{cite web|url=https://www.genialvegetal.net/-Linaire-striee-|title=Linaria repens - Linaire striée - Génial Végétal|website=genialvegetal.net|accessdate=2019-06-11}}</ref> It may also be poisonous.<ref name="genialvegetal"/>

==Habitat and distribution==

This species is found in stony wasteground, along walls, in arable situations and on railways. It grows to a maximum altitude of just over 2,300 metres.<ref name="naturespot"/><ref name="genialvegetal"/><ref name="brc">{{cite web|url=https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/linaria-repens|title=Linaria repens | Online Atlas of the British and Irish Flora|website=brc.ac.uk|accessdate=2019-06-11}}</ref>

It is found across western Europe and has been introduced to the east coast of the [[United States]].<ref name="usda">{{cite web|url=http://plants.usda.gov/plant-profile?symbol=LIRE3|website=plants.usda.gov|title=USDA Plant Profile for Linaria repens (striped toadflax) |access-date=2019-06-11}}</ref>

In the [[United Kingdom]], ''L. repens'' is theorised to be an [[archaeophyte]], i.e. introduced before 1492.<ref name="brc"/> It is rarely found in the east of England or in Ireland.

==Etymology==

The genus ''Linaria'' is named for the similarity of the plants' foliage to ''[[Linum]]'' (flax). The species epithet ''repens'' is Latin for 'creeping', referring to the growth habit of the plants. The 'pale' in the English common name refers to the colour of the flowers, in comparison with related species, and 'toadflax' is thought to refer to the plants' historical use to treat [[bubonic plague]], a false link having been drawn at some point between the words 'bubo' and ''[[Bufo]]'', which is Latin for [[Bufo bufo|toad]].<ref name="mobot">{{cite web|url=http://www.mobot.org/mobot/latindict/keyDetail.aspx?keyWord=repens|website=mobot.org|title=Missouri Botanical Garden - A Grammatical Dictionary of Botanical Latin |accessdate=2019-06-11}}</ref><ref name="google">{{cite book|title=Folk-Etymology|publisher=Ardent Media|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fXrlvr_kPXwC&pg=PA396|page=396|accessdate=2019-06-11}}</ref>
